exact_statement: Determine how large n must be as a function of r >= 2 so that there is an antichain in 2^[n] occupying n-3 distinct ranks and containing at least r members on every occupied rank.
scope_notes: Round four starts after the independently audited closure of the actual (++ -> ++) gamma4-negative rank-five branch in erdos-776-c1-round3.
The immediate unresolved target is adaptive recovery of actual (--)->(++) states that may remain negative at ranks five and six.
The K4,r9 odd-j family is a calibration theorem: proving rank-seven recovery for that one family is additional_local_branch and cannot promote the public problem.
Standalone success requires a uniform fixed-(k,r) recovery-rank theorem or an actual infinite nonrecovery counterfamily with a precise interface consequence.
Global success additionally requires a uniform pre-rank-42 seed, persistence/suffix composition, and the explicit public antichain-threshold implication.
